DAY 4

Oatmakers on day 4: the pipeline stands, the sites still run mixed versions

Today the whole group ships as one team, in one repo, to one live production gateway.
READ FIRST

How this works: you are contributors on one real, protected repo

  • Share your screen in the breakout room. exercises/lab.md is the source of truth; these slides mirror it.
  • No fork: everyone works in Mustry-Solutions/demo-oatmakers. Accept the collaborator invite and push your branches straight to it.
  • main is protected: a pull request, a green CI OK and one approval from someone else.
  • Production is pinned: build and verify locally, merge a reviewed PR, then tag and change release.yaml to deploy through Deploy.
  • Production is live and public: https://cloud.mustrysolutions.com. Verify through the public pages and the workflow logs.
  • Stuck? The Troubleshooting section of exercises/lab.md, then say so in the room.
RULES

Rules for shipping together to one live gateway

  1. Small PRs. One view, one migration pair, one module.
  2. Stage only what you changed: git add <your paths>, never git commit -am.
  3. One release PR in flight at a time. Say in the chat when you start, wait for Deploy to go green.
  4. A conflict in release.yaml is normal: rebase and keep every pin.
  5. Never lower a pin. Check whether your tag is already inside a higher one (Part 2).
  6. A pushed tag is permanent. Made a mistake? Fix it on main and cut the next number.
  7. Announce restarts: a module or a JAR restarts the production gateway.
  8. Leave the existing demo alone. Your screens, tags and tables carry your name or Course.
4 · a conflict in release.yaml
git fetch origin
git rebase origin/main
# fix release.yaml: keep every pin
# from main, re-apply only your line
git add release.yaml
git rebase --continue
git push --force-with-lease
THE PLAN

Four parts: local setup, your own project, the shared challenges, building on each other

  1. Part 0 · ±5 min · soloStart your local development gatewayRun the setup script for the development gateway and database.gate: open oatmakers in the Designer on localhost:8088
  2. Part 1 · ±20 min · soloCreate your own project and bring it liveAdd projects/<yourname>/ by PR, tag <yourname>@v1.0.0, pin it in release.yaml, watch Deploy ship it.gate: your view live on cloud.mustrysolutions.com
  3. Part 2 · ±35 min · groupFive challenges on the shared oatmakers projectA module, a JAR, a database with a migration and a referenced secret, a simulator with live tags, and history on top. Claim one each.gate: your challenge live via an oatmakers@ tag
  4. Part 3 · extra · groupBuild on each other's workA showcase view, a shared library at its own tag, crossing the challenges. You decide together who does what.gate: one PR that builds on someone else's work
START

Before you start: accept the invite, free the ports, clone next to the course repo

  1. Accept the invite from your GitHub notifications, or at github.com/Mustry-Solutions/demo-oatmakers/invitations. You get write access; no fork.
  2. Shut the lab 06 stack down (docker compose down in labs/06-secrets-db-and-modules/): it holds ports 8088 and 5432.
  3. Clone next to the course repo in ~/mustry-academy/, not inside cicd-for-ignition/. On Windows: in your WSL home, never under /mnt/c/.
cd ~/mustry-academy
git clone git@github.com:Mustry-Solutions/demo-oatmakers.git
cd demo-oatmakers
Your laptop runsWhereFed by
local gatewaylocalhost:8088your working tree (bind mount), admin / password
local databaselocalhost:5432login in local-development/secrets/
productioncloud.mustrysolutions.comDeploy, only when release.yaml changes
PART 0

Start your local development gateway and open the Designer

  1. Copy .env.example to .env. Clear the example value of LAB_USER and leave IGNITION_API_KEY empty.
  2. Run ./scripts/setup.sh. It starts the development gateway on 8088 and its database on 5432, generates your API key and applies local migrations.
  3. Sign in at localhost:8088 with admin / password. Open the Designer and the oatmakers project.
cp .env.example .env
# clear LAB_USER in .env
# leave IGNITION_API_KEY empty
./scripts/setup.sh
Part 0 gateThe local development gateway is running and you can open oatmakers in the Designer.
PART 1 · A

Build a project with your name locally and get it merged through review

  1. PR
  2. review
  3. merge
  4. tag
  5. pin by PR
  6. live
  1. Branch from a fresh main.
  2. Build it on the local gateway. In the Designer (localhost:8088, admin / password) create a project named <yourname>. Add one Perspective view that shows your name, make it the primary view of the / page in Page Configuration, save. git status shows projects/<yourname>/.
  3. Commit only your folder, push, open the PR. Wait for CI OK, then ask for an approval. Review comments? Fix and push again: same PR.
  4. Merge.
git switch main && git pull
git switch -c feature/<yourname>-project
# build projects/<yourname>/ in the Designer …
git status
git add projects/<yourname>/
git commit -m "feat: add <yourname> project with welcome view"
git push -u origin feature/<yourname>-project
ObserveProduction did not change: Deploy did not run, because release.yaml did not change.
PART 1 · B

Tag your release, pin it in release.yaml, and watch Deploy bring it live

  1. Tag the merged main: <yourname>@v1.0.0, and push the tag. Never tag your feature branch: a tag must point at a commit on main.
  2. Pin it: check the open PRs (one release PR in flight at a time), branch, add one line to release.yaml, stage only that file, push, PR, CI OK, approval, merge. Conflict with someone else's pin? Rebase and keep both lines.
  3. Watch it go live: Actions, Deploy on the demo-oatmakers runner. When it is green, open cloud.mustrysolutions.com/data/perspective/client/<yourname>/.
git switch main && git pull
git tag <yourname>@v1.0.0
git push origin <yourname>@v1.0.0

git switch -c pin/<yourname>-v1.0.0
# release.yaml
 projects:
   oatmakers:  v5.1.0
+  <yourname>: v1.0.0
git add release.yaml
git commit -m "release: pin <yourname> v1.0.0"
git push -u origin pin/<yourname>-v1.0.0
ObserveCI checks that <yourname>@v1.0.0 exists and sits on main. Pushed the tag after opening the PR? Checks, Re-run failed jobs.
Part 1 gateYour project merged through an approved PR, the tag <yourname>@v1.0.0 pushed, your line in release.yaml merged through an approved PR, your view live on production.
PART 2

Five challenges on the shared oatmakers project: claim one, ship it with the next free oatmakers@ tag

  1. Claim a challenge in the room. More people than challenges: pair up. Challenge 5 builds on 3 and 4.
  2. Work lands in projects/oatmakers/ plus services/, third-party-modules/, jar-files/jar/, db-migration/migrate/. Your views in Course/<yourname>/ with a page like /course/<yourname>, tags under Course/, tables prefixed course_.
  3. Verify locally before the PR: open your view on localhost:8088, exercise its behaviour and review git diff. Resolve problems before you merge and tag.
  4. Finished means live: merge, cut the next free oatmakers@ tag (from v5.1.0: a fix v5.1.1, a feature v5.2.0), pin it by PR.
git switch main && git pull
git fetch --tags
git tag -l 'oatmakers@*' --sort=-v:refname | head -3
git tag oatmakers@v5.2.0          # the next free number
git push origin oatmakers@v5.2.0
# rejected? someone took it: drop yours, take the next
git tag -d oatmakers@v5.2.0 && git fetch --tags
# release.yaml already pins a HIGHER oatmakers@ version?
# check whether your tag is inside it before you pin:
git merge-base --is-ancestor \
  oatmakers@v5.2.0 oatmakers@v5.3.0 && echo "already included"
ObserveAlready included: you are done, never pin backwards. No output: cut a new tag from the current main and pin that.
CHALLENGE 1

Add the Embr Charts module and build a chart screen

  1. Copy Embr-Charts-Ignition83-4.0.1.modl from the course repo's labs/06-secrets-db-and-modules/third-party-modules/ into demo-oatmakers's third-party-modules/. This is Embr Charts 4.0.1 for Ignition 8.3, module id com.mussonindustrial.embr.charts.
  2. Add the minimal entry on the right to services/modules.json: the lab 06 move.
  3. Recreate your local gateway (env vars only reach a new container). The repo's compose file already accepts this module id on your local gateway, so it installs headless and writes certFingerprint + licenseAgreementHash into your entry.
  4. Commit only your modules.json entry and the .modl.
  5. Build a Perspective screen with a chart from the module. Announce the restart in the chat before you merge the pin. Verify on production: your chart renders.
# services/modules.json, your entry
"com.mussonindustrial.embr.charts": {
  "filename": "/third-party-modules/Embr-Charts-Ignition83-4.0.1.modl",
  "onStartup": "enabled"
},

# a recreate, not a restart
docker compose up -d --force-recreate gateway
git diff services/modules.json   # the two values appeared
Already on main?If the entry already exists on main, keep its filename and version. Verify it runs on your local gateway at localhost:8088; recreate that gateway if needed, then build the screen.
CHALLENGE 2

Use the FastCSV JAR in a recipe-parsing function

  1. Download fastcsv-4.4.0.jar from Maven Central into jar-files/jar/ and add its row (source, sha256) to jar-files/jar/README.md: the lab 06 move. repo1.maven.org/maven2/de/siegmar/fastcsv/4.4.0/fastcsv-4.4.0.jar
  2. Load it locally: your gateway bind-mounts jar-files/jar/ into its JAR directory, so a restart loads it.
  3. A project script course/<yourname>/recipe, and a Perspective screen that calls it and shows oats | water | salt.
  4. Announce the restart in the chat before you merge the pin. Verify on production: the three fields show.
docker compose restart gateway   # JARs load at boot

# project script course/<yourname>/recipe
from de.siegmar.fastcsv.reader import CsvReader

def parseIngredients(line):
    records = list(CsvReader.builder().ofCsvRecord(line))
    return list(records[0].getFields())

# in a binding or script on your screen
course.<yourname>.recipe.parseIngredients("oats,water,salt")
CHALLENGE 3

Add a database connection with a referenced secret, a migration that seeds a table, and a view on the rows

  1. A connection named Course_<yourname> to jdbc:postgresql://postgres:5432/ignition (resolves locally and on production). Username: the plain string ignition. Password: the referenced secret POSTGRES_PASSWORD from the file secret provider named environment. You never see the value.
  2. The gateway adds a store-and-forward engine of the same name and status tags: stage them with the connection (paths on the right).
  3. A migration pair in db-migration/migrate/: .up.sql creates and seeds your course_ tables, .down.sql undoes exactly that. Always pairs.
  4. A Perspective view that queries the seeded rows. Verify on production: your page shows the rows.
# stage, under services/config/resources/core/ignition/
database-connection/Course_<yourname>/
store-and-forward-engine/Course_<yourname>/
tag-definition/System/Gateway/Database/Course_<yourname>/
tag-definition/System/Gateway/StoreAndForward/course_<yourname>/

scripts/migrate.sh up       # test it locally
scripts/migrate.sh down 1   # before you switch branches
Migration numberHigher than any on main at merge time. Same number as someone else after a rebase? Renumber yours.
CHALLENGE 4

Add a simulator device with a program, OPC tags on it and live values on a screen

  1. Add a Programmable Device Simulator named CourseSim (Connections, Devices). Device menu, Edit Program: add the two rows on the right (or load them as CSV).
  2. OPC tags in a Course/ folder of the default tag provider: OPC server Ignition OPC UA Server, item paths ns=1;s=[CourseSim]Ramp and ns=1;s=[CourseSim]Sine, type Float8. Use them on a Perspective screen.
  3. Stage your device, your tag folder and the status tags the gateway creates for the device.
  4. Verify on production: values changing live, on a gateway you never logged in to configure.
# the program: a ramp 0..100 every 60 s, a sine -50..50 every 30 s
Time Interval, Browse Path, Value Source, Data Type
0,"Ramp","ramp(0,100,60,1)","Double"
0,"Sine","sine(-50,50,30,1)","Double"
# stage, under services/config/resources/core/
com.inductiveautomation.opcua/device/CourseSim/
ignition/tag-definition/default/Course/
ignition/tag-definition/System/Gateway/Devices/CourseSim/
CHALLENGE 5

Historize the live tags with the TimescaleDB-Historian and chart them on a dashboard

  1. The TimescaleDB-Historian module already ships in third-party-modules/ and is registered in services/modules.json: you build on it, you do not install it.
  2. Create a historian named CourseHistorian of the module's TimescaleDB type that stores into the same plant database challenge 3's connection reads (jdbc:postgresql://postgres:5432/ignition, username ignition). Password: the referenced POSTGRES_PASSWORD.
  3. It comes with a store-and-forward engine of the same name: stage store-and-forward-engine/CourseHistorian/ and tag-definition/System/Gateway/StoreAndForward/coursehistorian/ with it. Never reuse a connection's name: they would share one engine.
  4. Enable tag history on challenge 4's tags, pointed at your historian, and build a dashboard view that charts that history.
  5. Verify on production: the chart fills up with history from the live tags.
Builds on challenges 3 and 4Start against their work as it lands on main. Merge conflicts are part of the challenge.
Part 2 gateYour challenge live on production through a reviewed PR, an oatmakers@ tag that contains it, and a release.yaml pin: yours, or a higher one you proved contains your tag.
PART 3 · EXTRA

Build on each other's work: decide as a group who does what, then ship it

A showcase view

One overview screen for oatmakers
  • Pull the group's work together on one screen: the chart, the live tags, the database rows.
  • Agree on the layout, then land it section by section, in small PRs.

A shared library

A parent project at its own version tag
  • Create an inheritable project projects/course-lib/ with something reusable: a styled component, a script function.
  • Tag course-lib@v1.0.0 and pin it. Make your Part 1 project inherit from it (project.json: "inheritable": true in course-lib, "parent": "course-lib" in yours), tag <yourname>@v1.1.0, pin that too.
  • Pin the parent before, or together with, its child.

Cross the challenges

Build on someone else, or get more reps
  • Historize more tags, add a migration on top of someone else's tables, put an Embr chart on the seeded data, call the recipe function from your view.
  • Or rebuild something that looks like another challenge, purely to train the move you want more practice on.
Stay currentEverything still ships the same way: small PR, quick review, next free tag, one release PR at a time. Pull main often and rebase your branch.
FIXES

Troubleshooting: ports, the trial, stray churn, migrations and a red release

SymptomFix
setup.sh says a port is in useStop the lab 06 stack, or set GATEWAY_PORT or POSTGRES_PORT in .env and re-run setup. Defaults: 8088 and 5432.
Blank Perspective pages, Designer disconnects, a deploy that worked failsThe trial lapsed: scripts/reset-trial.sh.
git status shows files you never touchedGateway churn (module fingerprints, resource.json stamps): do not stage it, see docs/resource-json-hygiene.html. Except the store-and-forward and status-tag folders of a device, connection or historian you added: stage those with it.
setup.sh or migrate.sh up: no migration found for version NA migration from your previous branch is still applied locally. On that branch: scripts/migrate.sh down 1 before switching branches.
CI OK is red on a release PROpen the failing job. Most often the pin points at a tag that was never pushed (git push origin <tag>) or not on main, or the YAML lost a line in a rebase. After pushing a tag: Checks, Re-run failed jobs.
Deploy is red, or production looks wrong after your releaseSay so in the chat straight away. The fix is the Revert button on the merged release PR, reviewed and merged as usual.
GATE

Definition of done for all four parts

  1. Part 0: the local development gateway is running and you can open oatmakers in the Designer.
  2. Part 1: projects/<yourname>/ merged through an approved PR, the tag <yourname>@v1.0.0, your line in release.yaml, and your view live on cloud.mustrysolutions.com.
  3. Part 2: your challenge merged and live on production via an oatmakers@ tag that contains it and a reviewed release.yaml pin.
  4. Part 3: at least one merged PR that builds on someone else's work, and at least one review (an approval or a comment) you gave someone else.
For the debriefWhen would you split this one repo, like option B? Who approves a production release at your plant? How would ten engineers share one version stream?

You shipped to a live production gateway through a protected, shared repo

  • A local development gateway where you built and verified each change before review and release.
  • Your own project, from git clone to live on production: a reviewed PR, a tag, a release.yaml line, a Deploy run.
  • Five challenges on one shared project: a module, a JAR, a database with a migration and a referenced secret, live tags from a simulator, and history on top.
  • One version stream shared by the whole group: tag races, rebases, merge conflicts and small fast PRs, like a real team on a real plant.
  • Every production deploy decided by one file, run by one labelled runner, approved by a human.
